app.title: OnKey
app.description: A singing trainer: learn to sing the songs you love, with the music you already play.

language.title: Language
language.label: Language
language.sub: The words OnKey shows. Automatic follows your computer’s language.
language.autoOs: {language} ({os, select, mac {your Mac’s language} other {this PC’s language}})
language.earlyNote: Lyrics for songs in {language} show without word-by-word timing for now. Want to help? <link>Improve this translation.</link>

mic.label: Microphone
mic.nowMissingMac: Now: {name}. The one you chose isn’t connected, so OnKey uses the Mac’s own input until it is.
mic.nowMissingPc: Now: {name}. The one you chose isn’t connected, so OnKey uses {input} until it is.
mic.noneMissingMac: <warn>No microphone is connected.</warn> The one you chose isn’t connected, so OnKey uses the Mac’s own input until it is.
mic.noneMissingPc: <warn>No microphone is connected.</warn> The one you chose isn’t connected, so OnKey uses {input} until it is.
mic.moreMac: Automatic uses your Mac’s input (System Settings → Sound), but not Bluetooth headphones’ mic while the Mac has its own, so the music stays at full quality in them. Setup’s mic check and your takes use the same one. Virtual devices other apps add (Krisp, Loopback, BlackHole, Zoom, Teams) are listed apart: pick one only to sing through it on purpose, as it gives OnKey that app’s sound, not your mic’s.
mic.morePc: Automatic uses {input} ({soundInput}). Setup’s mic check and your takes use the same one.

output.label: Output
output.now: Now: {name}. Change it in {os, select, mac {System Settings → Sound} other {{sound}}}.

setup.title: Run setup again
setup.sub: Permissions and the mic check, as on the first day.

shortcuts.next: Next song, or skip to the singing
shortcuts.blind: Show or hide the notes (Blind take)
shortcuts.mini: Mini mode: a small lyrics bar on top of other apps

updates.unsupportedMac: Development build: it doesn’t update itself.
updates.unsupportedPc: This test build doesn’t update itself: install a new one over it when there is one.
updates.waiting: OnKey {version} is installed when this song is over, then OnKey restarts.
updates.ready: OnKey {version} is ready. Restart to update, or it’s installed when you quit.
updates.official: OnKey {version} is out from the original project, at singonkey.app. This copy was built from source, so it doesn’t update itself.
updates.currentSource: You have the latest version. This copy was built from source: it says when a new version is out, and doesn’t update itself.
updates.updateFailed: Couldn’t update to OnKey {version}. Check now tries again.
updates.updateFailedWhy: Couldn’t update to OnKey {version} ({error}). Check now tries again.
updates.checkFailed: Couldn’t check for updates just now.
updates.checkFailedWhy: Couldn’t check for updates just now ({error}).

auto.title: Check for updates automatically
auto.sub: Once a day, in the background. It never interrupts a song.
auto.more: OnKey asks GitHub for a newer version and downloads it in the background. It’s installed when you restart or quit.

scoring.title: Scoring
scoring.label: Scoring level
scoring.more: Vibrato is fine: your pitch is judged by the middle of its wobble. Every score in OnKey is shown at this level, your earlier takes too: they’re scored again from your singing as it was kept.
scoring.moreRelaxed: Every score in OnKey is shown at this level, your earlier takes too: they’re scored again from your singing as it was kept.

control.title: Let OnKey control
control.introMac: On by default: OnKey reads what’s playing and where (exact, instant positions), and can play, pause, seek and start songs. Nothing else. macOS asks once for each.
control.introPc: On by default: OnKey reads what’s playing and where, and can play, pause, seek and start songs. Nothing else.
control.introAsking: OnKey follows Spotify and Apple Music by asking them, so it controls them already.

spotify.title: Spotify
spotify.missing: Spotify isn’t installed on this {os, select, mac {Mac} other {PC}}.
spotify.sub: Start, pause and skip songs in Spotify from OnKey.

music.title: Apple Music
music.missingMac: The Music app isn’t on this Mac.
music.missingPc: The Apple Music app isn’t on this PC.
music.subMac: The same for the Music app (songs in your library).
music.subPc: The same for the Apple Music app.

youtube.title: YouTube in your browser
youtube.subMac: Read and control the YouTube tab in Chrome, Brave, Edge or Safari.
youtube.moreMac: Needs “Allow JavaScript from Apple Events” turned on in the browser. While it’s on (and for 10 minutes after you open a YouTube song from OnKey), OnKey listens to your browser’s sound, whatever it is, calls and podcasts included: sound it doesn’t recognise may go to Shazam as a short fingerprint (never the audio) unless Shazam is off below.
youtube.subPc: Follow songs playing in Chrome, Edge, Firefox, Brave, Opera or Vivaldi.
youtube.morePc: From what the browser tells {os} is playing; OnKey can play, pause and seek them there. Until a song is learned its position can be a little less exact than Spotify’s.

control.listenOnlyMac: OnKey is listening only: it follows songs by their sound, and doesn’t touch any app. Positions are a little less exact, and it can’t start or restart songs. Turning an app off here doesn’t take back macOS’s permission: that’s in System Settings → Privacy & Security → Automation.
control.listenOnlyPc: OnKey is listening only: it follows songs by their sound, and doesn’t touch any app. On {os} that’s only songs it has already learned: new ones are named by {apps} while they’re on here.
control.allOff: With all of these off, OnKey follows songs by their sound alone.

naming.title: Naming songs
naming.pc: Songs you’ve sung before are recognised on this PC from their sound. New songs are named by Spotify, Apple Music or your browser (with YouTube on), from what they say is playing. Nothing is sent anywhere to name a song.

shazam.title: Use Shazam to name new songs
shazam.sub: Names new songs from a short fingerprint of the sound, not the audio.
shazam.more: Songs you’ve sung before are recognised on this Mac. New songs from Spotify and Apple Music are named by the app itself while OnKey may control it; Shazam names the rest. When off, nothing is sent to Shazam and only songs already learned on this Mac are recognised there. Album covers are still looked up by artist and title in Apple’s iTunes catalogue.
shazam.warn: With Spotify and Apple Music off, new songs can only be learned with Shazam on. Songs already learned still work.

show.title: Show lyrics
show.sub: From LRCLIB, a free community lyrics database.
show.more: When off, OnKey doesn’t ask LRCLIB for any, and you sing to the notes alone: the pitch guide and your score work as usual.

breaks.title: Remind me to rest my voice
breaks.sub: A quiet reminder to take a break after about 35 minutes of singing.
breaks.more: A 20-minute pause from singing starts the count again.

fadeGuide.title: Fade the guide on songs you know
fadeGuide.sub: Your pitch line fades while you’re on the note, so you listen to yourself more.
fadeGuide.more: It starts once you’ve sung a song well (your best 80 or more, or your last two takes 75 or more). The better you know it, the fainter it gets; more than a semitone off, it shows as usual. The notes always stay, and you can bring the full guide back for any take.

battery.title: Save battery while singing
battery.sub: On battery, the notes are drawn a little less often. Still smooth.
battery.more: 30 times a second instead of 60: half the drawing work for your Mac.

keepModels.title: Keep learning models ready
keepModels.sub: New songs are learned faster, but OnKey uses more memory.
keepModels.more: About 1.5 GB more, also while you sing songs OnKey already knows. Off, the models are loaded when a new song is learned and let go after. On by default on {os, select, mac {Macs} other {PCs}} with 32 GB or more.

about.title: About

report.title: Report a problem
report.subMac: Save OnKey’s logs and timings as a zip to attach to a GitHub issue. You see what’s in it first; no lyrics or audio, nothing uploaded.
report.subPc: Save OnKey’s logs and timings as one zip on your Desktop, to attach to a message or a GitHub issue. You see what’s in it first; no lyrics or audio, nothing uploaded.

guides.title: Guides and help
guides.sub: How OnKey works, scoring, fixing problems and singing comfortably, on singonkey.app.

discord.title: Join OnKey’s Discord
discord.sub: Ask questions, report a song that’s out of step, and suggest ideas.

madeBy.title: Made by Daniel Murrell
madeBy.tagline: Saving shower singers from themselves since 2026

fairUse.title: Using OnKey fairly
fairUse.sub: What OnKey is for, and how to share your singing without sharing the music.

licences.title: Open-source licences
licences.sub: The models, data, fonts and libraries OnKey is built on, and their licences.

about.footer: For personal practice at home. What OnKey learns stays on this {os, select, mac {Mac} other {PC}}: please keep it to yourself, and don’t post takes or screen recordings with the music in them.

relaxed.name: Relaxed
relaxed.about: Forgiving: full credit within half a semitone. Good for beginners and children.

steady.name: Steady
steady.about: Tighter pitch and timing, for singers who are mostly in tune.

pro.name: Pro
pro.about: Tight, for trained singers: a quarter of a semitone for full credit.

mic.deniedMac: Your singing isn’t heard or scored until it can. In System Settings → Privacy & Security → Microphone, turn on OnKey.

lyricsDown.body: LRCLIB, the free lyrics service OnKey uses, isn’t working at the moment. The notes still show, and the words join them if it comes back during the song. A song learned meanwhile gets its words the next time you sing it.

To fix it, download OnKey again and {os, select, pc {install it over this one} other {replace the app in Applications}}: your songs and takes are kept.

modelsBroken.body: Its pitch model, which comes inside the app, couldn’t load{hasError, select, yes { ({error})} other {}}. To fix it, download OnKey again and replace the app in Applications: your songs and takes are kept.

welcome.title: Welcome to OnKey
welcome.lead: Learn to sing the songs you love, with the music you already play.
welcome.play: Play a song in your music app, as you always do. OnKey listens to the music playing on your {os, select, mac {Mac} other {PC}} and follows along by itself.
welcome.learn: The first time a song plays, OnKey learns the singer’s melody. From then on you see every note coming, and where you’re sharp or flat.
welcome.privacyPc: OnKey never saves the music it listens to. Your singing recordings stay on this PC so you can hear your takes back. Songs are named on this PC too, from what your music app says is playing: nothing is sent to name them.
welcome.privacyMac: OnKey never saves the music it listens to. Your singing recordings stay on this Mac so you can hear your takes back. To name a new song, listening mode sends Apple’s Shazam a short fingerprint of the music app’s sound (not the audio).
welcome.entitled: OnKey is for practising at home with music you’re entitled to play. The melodies it learns are for your own practice, so keep them to yourself.
welcome.macosOld: OnKey needs macOS 14.2 or later to hear other apps. Update macOS in System Settings → General → Software Update.

permissions.title: Two permissions
permissions.sub: macOS asks once for each. You can change them later in System Settings → Privacy & Security.

audio.title: System audio recording
audio.why: To hear the music playing on your Mac, so OnKey can learn the melody. OnKey never saves the music or sends it; to name a song it doesn't know, a short fingerprint of it (not the audio) can go to Apple's Shazam.
audio.hint: Open Screen & System Audio Recording and turn on OnKey under System Audio Recording Only.

permissions.reopen: If macOS asks to quit and reopen OnKey after you allow something, do. Setup carries on where you left off.
permissions.restricted: Your Mac's settings don't allow this. Ask whoever manages it.

musicApps.title: Let OnKey follow Spotify and Apple Music
musicApps.why: So lyrics and notes are in the right place from the first second, and OnKey can play and restart songs for you.
musicApps.scope: It can read what’s playing and where, and play, pause and seek. Nothing else. macOS asks once for each app.
musicApps.waitingMac: Waiting for macOS. If it’s asking about Spotify or Apple Music (its question can open behind this window), answer it. No question? Carry on: macOS asks the first time you play a song there.
musicApps.noAnswer: macOS hasn’t had an answer yet. If its question is showing, answer it; otherwise it asks the first time you play a song there.

state.notRunning: macOS asks when you first play a song in it

micCheck.title: Can OnKey hear you?
micCheck.micOffPc: Windows has the microphone turned off for apps. In Windows Settings → Privacy & security → Microphone, turn on Microphone access and Let desktop apps access your microphone.
micCheck.micFirst: OnKey needs the microphone first: go back to allow it.
micCheck.noMicDevice: No microphone is connected. Connect one, or choose one in {soundInput}.
micCheck.say: Say something, or sing a note.
micCheck.device: Listening to {device}. You can choose another in Settings.
micCheck.headphones: Headphones give the steadiest scores. Laptop speakers work too: OnKey takes the music out of what the mic hears.

ready.title: You're set
ready.lead: Play a song in your music app and start singing. The first play of each song teaches OnKey the melody.

tip.toEnd: Let a song play to the end. If OnKey hears only part of it, it learns the rest the next time it plays.
tip.talk: Talk or sing along as you like. OnKey learns from the music app’s sound, not your mic.
tip.volumePc: Keep the music app’s own volume at about a quarter or more.
tip.learnPc: Learning runs on this PC for a few minutes after the song ends. Keep listening meanwhile.
tip.volumeMac: Keep the music app’s own volume at about a quarter or more. Your Mac’s volume can be anything, even off.
tip.learnMac: Learning runs on your Mac for a couple of minutes after the song ends, longer on Macs with 8 GB of memory. Keep listening meanwhile.

ready.quickest: Quickest start: play the OnKey starter playlist and leave it on for half an hour.
ready.comfortable: Sing at a comfortable volume: OnKey scores your pitch, not how loud you are. Rest when your voice tires, and stop if your throat hurts.

controlPrompt.bodyAllow: OnKey is listening to {app}, not controlling it. To start songs, skip to the singing and pause from OnKey, it needs your permission.{os, select, mac { macOS will ask you once too.} other {}}
controlPrompt.bodyCant: OnKey follows {app} by listening only. Play, pause and skip there.
controlPrompt.browserPc: OnKey can then follow songs in your browser, and play, pause and seek them there.
controlPrompt.browserMac: This is the bigger permission: OnKey can then read and control the YouTube tab in your browser, and listens to your browser’s sound, whatever it is (calls too): sound it doesn’t recognise may go to Shazam as a short fingerprint, never the audio. Your browser also needs “Allow JavaScript from Apple Events” turned on.
controlPrompt.changeLater: You can change this any time in Settings.

systemAudio.summary: How to let OnKey record system audio on a Mac. In System Settings, open Privacy & Security, choose Screen & System Audio Recording, and turn on OnKey under System Audio Recording Only. If macOS asks, choose Quit & Reopen. OnKey opens again with system audio recording ticked and setup carries on.

learnSong.summary: OnKey learning a song. A song plays once to the end in a music player while sound waves flow into OnKey and its melody is drawn as note bars. A couple of minutes after it ends, a Learning ring turns into a green check: Learned. The next time the song plays, the notes scroll by with the singer's green pitch line riding on them and the lyrics underneath.

steps.s2: It’s left out of the score, for every take of the song

leaveOut.ariaLabel: Animation of a pitch graph for one take of a song. Purple bars show the notes the score expects and a line shows what the singer sang, green where it matches. For one stretch the purple bars jump up high, following a backing vocal, while the singer stays on the melody and the line turns amber. A cursor drags across that stretch to select it and clicks "Leave it out of the score". The stretch turns to grey stripes, the score rises from {before} to {after}, and the same stretch is left out for every take of the song.
leaveOut.leaveOutButton: Leave it out of the score

steps.s0: On speakers, the song gets into your recording
steps.s1: With headphones, it's just your voice

speakers.label: Two short scenes. On laptop speakers, the backing song spills out and curls into the microphone, so the recording mixes your voice with the music. With headphones, the music stays in your ears and the recording is just your voice.

fadeDemo.ariaLabel: Four takes of the same song as note lanes: Take 1, 3, 5 and 8. The purple notes stay the same in every take. Your green pitch line is bright in Take 1 and fainter each take while it's on the note; in Take 5 it slips more than a semitone off for a moment and that part shows in full, in red. A Full guide switch brings the whole line back.

report.introPc: OnKey puts its records in one zip file on your Desktop for you to attach to a message: its log for the last three days, a summary of each play, and a summary of this PC, its sound and the music apps it followed. fairUse.title: Using OnKey fairly
fairUse.intro: OnKey is for practising at home, with music you’re entitled to play. Please:

keep.title: Keep what it learns to yourself.
keep.body: Its transcription of each song’s melody is for your practice, so don’t share or publish it. Sharing OnKey itself is welcome.

share.title: To share a take, use Share on its page.
share.body: It makes a short video of your voice and your pitch line, with no music, and you can add the song from Instagram’s own music library, which is licensed for this. Headphone takes are best: sung on speakers, some of the song is in your recording. Don’t post screen recordings with the music playing.

venue.title: Use a licensed karaoke service for a bar or an event.
venue.body: OnKey’s lyrics come from a free community database.

modify.title: Don’t modify OnKey to save the music.

fairUse.contact: OnKey never saves the music it listens to. Rights holders can reach me at <email>hello@singonkey.app</email>.
